historical-evidence.json.subject: Euston Arch, London, 1873

sources.usedFor: Original Doric gateway architect Philip Hardwick; EUSTON name only carved in 1874, therefore omitted in 1873.
Surviving archival view of the propylaeum.
Two front fluted Doric columns between rectangular antae; two rear columns; heavy triangular pediment, flanking lodges and gates. Later lettering deliberately not copied.
Flanking lodges and ornate gates, pedestrian/vehicle gateway before station not railway track through portico.

historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Reconstructed 1873 condition based on surviving later archival photographs and railway chronology; incidental lodge details, dress and passerby identities illustrative, not documented individuals. No EUSTON lettering in 1873.

historical-evidence.json.subject: Newgate Prison, George Dance the Younger building, London 1873

sources.usedFor: George Dance prison, deeply rusticated walls enclosing three internal courts, archive photographs and measured drawing on PDF pages 7-8.
Building identification and museum collection painting of the intact late Georgian prison.
Wood doors reinforced with sheet iron and iron studs, dating to 1770s rebuilding.

sources.authority: 1894 Descriptive Album of London historical photograph, reproduced by Brisk
sources.usedFor: Direct period visual evidence for facade massing; not a source for modern historical claims.
Letter carrier blue coat and trousers by 1860 and all letter carriers uniformed by 1872; red piping.

historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: The 1873 reconstruction uses a later period photograph of the same George Dance building. Concealed court/roof arrangement and incidental uniforms are interpretive; two people are fictional. Exterior prison doorway is a plausible context, not a claim the museum retained door was at this exact entrance.

historical-evidence.json.subject: Greenwich Palace / Placentia, London circa 1530

sources.usedFor: Historic Tudor palace location, early sixteenth-century rebuilding and court arrangement.
Henry VII red-brick rebuilding, Henry VIII additions, royal arrival by water and Thames pier; museum historical Placentia engraving.

sources.authority: Old Royal Naval College historical site organisation
sources.usedFor: Tudor royal palace context and Henry VIII occupancy.

sources.authority: Royal Museums Greenwich historical engraving PAI5655
sources.usedFor: Long riverfront facade, towers, Tudor windows and roof massing; later historical depiction rather than exact 1530 survey.

historical-evidence.json.uncertainty: Lost palace reconstructed approximately from historic depictions, surviving archaeology and museum descriptions. Exact 1530 wing/turret/window details and court boat/dress are interpretive; no claim of exact surveyed building or identifiable historical individuals. Later Queen House/Naval College deliberately excluded.

research.json.uncertainty: Interpretive historical reconstruction: surviving plan and drawings determine massing; precise statues, marble colours and complete upper tiers uncertain. Not a survey reconstruction.
